name: Augustus Pablo
hook: A schoolroom melodica became the lead voice of dub, on records King Tubby stripped down to almost nothing.

blurb.age7: Augustus Pablo played a little keyboard you blow into, called a melodica, and it became one of the main sounds of dub music.
blurb.age13: Born Horace Swaby, Pablo learned the melodica at school in Kingston and used it as a lead instrument on reggae instrumentals, which nobody else was doing. He worked closely with King Tubby, who remixed Pablo's rhythms into some of the most famous dub records ever made.
blurb.adult: Pablo (Horace Swaby) built a body of work almost entirely on the melodica, an instrument treated as a schoolroom novelty everywhere else in popular music. His 1976 album with King Tubby, 'King Tubbys Meets Rockers Uptown,' is widely considered one of the defining dub records, pairing Pablo's minor-key melodica lines with Tubby's spare, cavernous mixing.

signatureTracks.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Pablo's melodica over a Tubby mix stripped to drum, bass, and echo; the melodica occupies the space a vocal would normally take.

signatureTracks.title: East of the River Nile
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A full album of melodica-led dub, and the clearest showcase of Pablo as a bandleader rather than a guest voice.
